'''Horst Herrlich''' (11 September 1937, in [[Berlin]] – 13 March 2015, in [[Bremen]]) was a German mathematician, known as a pioneer of [[categorical topology]].

==Education and career==
Horst Herrlich received his PhD in 1962 with thesis ''Ordnungsfähigkeit topologischer Räume'' (Orderability of topological spaces) under Karl Peter Grotemeyer and [[Alexander Dinghas]] at the [[Free University of Berlin]],<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=21562}}</ref> where he also received his [[habilitation]] in 1965 with a thesis on E-compact spaces (introduced by Stanisław Mrówka in 1958).<ref>{{cite journal|author=Mrówka, S.|title=Further results on E-compact space. I|journal=[[Acta Mathematica]]|volume=120|issue=1|year=1968|pages=161–185|doi=10.1007/BF02394609|doi-access=free}}</ref>

From 1971 to 2002 Herrlich was a professor of mathematics with a focus on [[general topology]] and [[category theory]] at the [[University of Bremen]]. He was part of the editorial staff for the third volume ''Deskriptive Mengenlehre und Topologie'' of the collected works of [[Felix Hausdorff]].<ref>{{cite journal|title=Book review of ''Felix Hausdorff—Gesammelte Werke''|author=Gray, Jeremy|authorlink=Jeremy Gray (mathematician)|journal=[[Bull. Amer. Math. Soc.]]|volume=51|year=2014|pages=169–172|doi=10.1090/S0273-0979-2013-01424-1|doi-access=free}}</ref>

He was an Invited Speaker of the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] in 1974 in [[Vancouver]].<ref>{{cite book|author=Herrlich, Horst|title=Proceedings of the International Congress of Mathematicians, held in Vancouver, August 21—29, 1974|chapter=Topological Structures|volume=2|pages=63–66}}</ref> He is regarded as a founder of categorical topology, which deals with general topology using the methods of category theory.
